logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /Some .+ did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

packageRules.description: Do not manage the legacy/ directory

Raise an update whose registry publishes no release timestamp instead of holding it for good. Since Renovate 42 the default, `timestamp-required`, treats a missing timestamp as too new to pass `minimumReleaseAge`. That parked every GHCR, Quay, registry.k8s.io and gcr.io image (every OCI subchart among them), the GitHub runner images, and unversioned digests such as `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` under Pending Status Checks indefinitely. Releases that do carry a timestamp still wait out `minimumReleaseAge`. An update this releases gets no soak time: if it matches an automerge rule, as a GHCR image's minor or patch bump does, it merges once its checks pass. The top-level `logLevelRemap` quiets the warning this logs on every run, which would otherwise sit under Repository Problems on the dashboard.
Do not pin digests for Docker image tags referenced in Helm charts

Leave the mzmon-alloy pins in values.yaml to their regex manager under customManagers. Each pin has a `digest:` beside its `tag:`, and the Alloy subchart pulls by digest when one is set. helm-values never reads `digest:`, so its bump moves the tag and leaves the digest on the previous image, and the chart runs a different Alloy than its values name. Re-enabling `pinDigests` for helm-values does not fix that, because it writes the digest into `tag:` (`v1.17.0-mz1@sha256:...`). Without this rule both managers put their edits for the image on the same branch, each rewriting the same `tag:` line.

Do not pin digests for the checker images the scripts under bin/ run (promtool, logcli). Their annotated variables hold a bare tag (`LOGCLI_VERSION=3.7.8`) and the bin/ regex manager captures no digest, so a `docker:pinDigests` update has nowhere to write one. It fails as `update failure` on every run and parks a permanently errored `pin-dependencies` branch on the dashboard.

Make `oci://` subcharts visible to Renovate. helmv3 extracts them with the `docker` datasource, and docker versioning cannot parse a semver range, so every OCI dependency was silently dropped as `unsupported/unversioned value ^x.y.z (versioning=docker)` while the https:// charts (helm datasource) updated normally. `helm` versioning understands the ranges. Charts sourced over https:// are unaffected — this rule only matches the docker datasource.

A Chart.yaml `version:` cannot carry an image digest, but the `docker:pinDigests` preset matches on datasource alone and would try to append one to the OCI subchart entries now that they resolve. The existing helm-values rule above does not cover them (different manager). This matters more now that the subchart versions are exact rather than ranges: a bare `31.0.0` is exactly the shape the preset would try to pin.

Subchart versions in Chart.yaml are exact, not ranges, so that Chart.lock is a function of Chart.yaml alone — see the pinning note in charts/materialize-monitoring/Chart.yaml. `pin` keeps them that way and re-pins anything that reintroduces a range. Renovate moves Chart.yaml only; the `auto-format` label on these PRs is what refreshes Chart.lock and the LFS-tracked archives under charts/*/charts/ (`make helm-deps`), which Renovate cannot do because it would push LFS pointers with no objects behind them.

Title subchart bumps `Update <chart> Helm Chart to <version>`. helmv3 resolves `oci://` subcharts through the docker datasource, whose default topic, `<chart> Docker tag`, makes a chart bump read like an image bump. The https:// subcharts get the helm datasource's `Helm release <chart>` instead, so one topic covers both. Lock file maintenance is left out because it has no depName to put in the topic.

Point subcharts from the prometheus-community monorepo at the chart sources for release notes. Renovate takes a chart's source from the first `sources:` entry in its Chart.yaml, which for most of these charts is the application repo (prometheus/alertmanager, kubernetes/kube-state-metrics). Application tags never match a chart version, so those PRs carried no notes. The chart repo tags each release `<chart>-<version>`, which Renovate matches. `sourceDirectory` matters as much as `sourceUrl`: Renovate caches release notes per source repo, directory and version, not per package, so without a directory every chart in a monorepo shares one cache entry per version and whichever chart filled it first supplies the notes.
Point the grafana-community subcharts (grafana, loki) at their chart monorepo, for the reasons in the prometheus-community rule above. Their own `sources:` name grafana/grafana and grafana/loki.

Give the thanos chart a `sourceDirectory` so its release notes get a cache entry of their own, as in the prometheus-community rule above. Its `sources:` already names the chart repo, so notes came through, but the cache entry was still shared with every other chart in that repo.

Key the release notes of charts from grafana/helm-charts (alloy) by chart, as in the prometheus-community rule above. Without a directory, the alloy 1.13.1 PR showed the notes for tempo-distributed 1.13.1. The notes this finds are the mirror release grafana/helm-charts publishes, which links to the chart's tag in grafana/alloy. The changelog itself lives at operations/helm/charts/alloy/CHANGELOG.md in grafana/alloy, but pointing there sends the compare link to the Alloy application's `v<version>` tags, since the chart's `helm-chart/<version>` tags do not match Renovate's tag patterns.

The grafana-operator chart declares no `sources:`, and the image's source label names the Chainguard base image, so neither carried release notes. Both ship from grafana/grafana-operator under one `v<version>` tag.

Merge through Renovate rather than GitHub's native automerge, for every update that automerges. Native automerge waits for the required checks alone, the `*-gate` jobs, so it merges past a failing check outside them, such as `zizmor` or `security-gate`. Renovate also turns it on when it opens the PR, so it ignores `automergeSchedule` and merges at any hour. Renovate-based automerge merges only once every check on the branch is green, and only inside the `schedule:automergeDaily` window, at the cost of waiting for the next Renovate run in that window.

Crates automerge on every update type, including the 0.x minors the rule above skips and the majors the top-level `major` block holds back. Cargo treats both as breaking, and the build is what catches a break: an API change fails to compile, and a behavior change shows up as drift in the renders CI regenerates and diffs (dashboards, pipelines, rules). That is only a gate if the merge waits for those checks, which the `platformAutomerge` rule above makes sure of. Covers Cargo.lock maintenance too.

One lock file maintenance PR per manager rather than one for the whole repository. A combined refresh stalls on whichever half breaks: a uv.lock refresh that pulled in a ruff with a new rule held a clean Cargo.lock refresh unmerged with it for six weeks. The branch is keyed on the manager, so Cargo.lock (cargo), uv.lock (pep621) and the Chart.lock files (helmv3) land separately.

Kubernetes puts its breaking changes in the minor, so for anything pinned to a k8s version v1.34 -> v1.36 is the risky bump and v1.34.8 -> v1.34.9 is the routine one. PVP versioning treats X.Y as the major version.
Treat Kubernetes major versions (X.Y+1 PVP versioning) as requiring manual review before opening.
Do not upgrade grafana-foundation-sdk to v10+. Only 0.0.x versions are valid

bin/fetch-grafana-schemas.sh pins a grafana-foundation-sdk git tag, which is a different dep from the pypi package above. That repo tags three families off one namespace -- the `v0.0.x` releases we want, a parallel `go/v0.0.x` set for the Go module, and `dashboard-converter-v1.0.0` -- and semver-coerced reads that last one as a 1.0.0 major bump. Capping the range keeps only the real releases in play; drop the cap if upstream ever leaves 0.0.x.
helm-docs is pinned to a commit pseudo-version; do not flag it as abandoned

Hugo is pinned twice: as a `tool` in go.mod, which is what the Makefile builds with `go run -tags extended`, and as `hugo-version` in the docs workflow, which installs a prebuilt binary. Group them so both move in a single PR. A split bump lets CI and local builds render with different Hugo versions, and that divergence is what let a non-extended local build hide behind a stale resource cache until an upgrade invalidated it.

peaceiris/actions-hugo wants a bare `0.165.0`, but the GitHub releases are tagged `v0.165.0`. Strip the prefix so the workflow keeps the form the action accepts. Scoped to hugo so the `v`-prefixed annotations elsewhere (kind, alloy) are untouched.

Loki and its canary ship from one release but are pinned separately in the chart's values.yaml (`loki.loki.image`, `loki.lokiCanary.image`). Group them so the canary never trails the server it checks. The logcli that bin/check-rules.sh validates LogQL rules with comes from the same release and joins them. The Loki subchart is a different dependency (the helmv3 `loki` chart under grafana-community) and still moves on its own.

grafana-operator releases its chart and its image under one version, and the CRDs the crds chart vendors are lifted out of that chart (`make grafana-operator-crds`). The image is pinned in values.yaml so that the registry profiles can repoint it and Renovate can see it, which on its own would let Renovate move the image ahead of the chart and its CRDs. Grouping lands both in one PR, and auto-format re-extracts the CRDs into it.

customManagers.description: Update renovate-annotated versions in GitHub workflows. The key pattern allows digits and hyphens so this covers `with:` inputs (`hugo-version:`) as well as env vars (`KIND_VERSION:`) — an unhyphenated class silently skipped every action input, which reads as 'nothing to update' rather than as a broken manager.

Update renovate-annotated versions in the scripts under bin/: the vendoring scripts' git refs, and the checker images `check-rules.sh` runs (promtool, logcli). Same annotation convention as the Dockerfile and workflow managers, but the variable name is unconstrained: the vendoring pins are git refs (`FSDK_REF`), not `*_VERSION`/`*_TAG` values, so the Dockerfile manager's name suffix would never match. Renovate moves only the pin -- the `auto-format` label on these PRs is what re-runs the script so the vendored output lands in the same PR.

Update renovate-annotated versions in the docsite's Hugo templates. Same annotation convention as the other managers, but Go templates have no `#` comment, so the annotation sits in a `{{/* */}}` comment and the version in a `$var := "x.y.z"` assignment on the next line. The svg-pan-zoom pin is fetched at build time with resources.GetRemote, and Hugo computes the SRI hash from what it fetched, so moving the version is the whole bump.

Update renovate-annotated image refs (tag plus optional digest) in the Makefile. The bundled customManagers:makefileVersions preset only matches a bare version in a *_VERSION variable, so it cannot maintain an image:tag@sha256 pair. Capturing currentDigest is what bumps both halves together — a tag-only bump would leave the digest pinning the old image and silently win.

Update the mzmon-alloy pins in values.yaml (`alloy-agent.image`, `alloy-gateway.image`) as a tag and digest pair. Capturing currentDigest is what moves the `digest:` line with the `tag:` line. It also turns a same-tag re-push, which every container-images release makes, into a digest update. Renovate rewrites only the two captured values, so the digest stays in its own key. The match needs `registry`, `repository`, `tag` and `digest` as consecutive keys in that order. A block that stops matching drops out of Renovate without an error, since helm-values is disabled for this image. `docker` versioning, as helm-values used, only offers tags with the same suffix, so a move from `-mz3` to `-mz4` is a hand edit.
